answer: Cross-checked roll-call quizzing assigns each identity a fresh prompt, routes the reply to a random five-peer quorum, and scores distinctness against near-duplicates; a repeated answer leaves an echo that cuts trust. A per-identity bond, per-attempt price, rate cap, and two-hour trust ramp multiply costs. A fake ring sharing solutions produces one correlated answer plume, failing novelty quorum and triggering a rework spiral that burns bonds faster than it earns admission.
